
ADD-QUESTION
Add a question to a work unit during Example Mapping discovery phase

WHEN TO USE
  Use during Example Mapping in the specifying phase when you encounter uncertainties, ambiguities, or need clarification from the human about requirements, rules, or expected behavior.

USAGE
  fspec add-question <workUnitId> <question>

ARGUMENTS
  <workUnitId> (required)
    Work unit ID (e.g., AUTH-001)
  <question> (required)
    The question text (use @human: prefix for human-directed questions)

OPTIONS
  No options available

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Use @human: prefix for questions directed at the human (e.g., "@human: Should we support OAuth?")
  • Ask one focused question at a time rather than multiple questions in one
  • Frame questions to elicit concrete examples or rules
  • Questions should be answered before moving to testing phase

TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Add question during discovery
  2. Human answers question
  3. Convert answer to rule or assumption
  4. Continue until no questions remain
  5. Move to testing phase

EXAMPLES
  1. Add question during Example Mapping
  $ fspec add-question AUTH-001 "@human: Should we support OAuth providers?"
  ✓ Question added successfully

  2. Answer the question (index 0)
  $ fspec answer-question AUTH-001 0 --answer "Yes, support Google and GitHub OAuth"
  ✓ Answered question: "@human: Should we support OAuth providers?"
  Answer: "Yes, support Google and GitHub OAuth"

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec answer-question
  fspec add-rule
  fspec add-example
  fspec generate-scenarios
  fspec show-work-unit

NOTES
  • Questions must be answered before transitioning from specifying to testing
  • Use show-work-unit to see all questions and their status
  • Questions capture uncertainties that become rules or assumptions once answered
